nabidky.nazev: Memory in public space: memorials, monuments and cemeteries as a planning task

nabidky.nazev: Basic characterization of construction materials
anotace: We offer comprehensive characterization of construction materials, raw materials, individual components and composite materials using modern analytical and microscopy methods. We determine phase and chemical composition and evaluate the microstructure and basic physical properties of materials. Thanks to our extensive instrumentation and experience in materials characterization, we can offer not only the measurements themselves but also the design of a suitable analytical procedure and expert interpretation of the results.

We specialize in particular in the characterization of cementitious and other inorganic binders, mortars and concretes, ceramic and refractory materials, aggregates, mineral raw materials, powders and bulk materials, and waste materials and secondary raw materials usable in construction. However, we also provide analyses for a wider range of materials, and, following an individual consultation, their scope can be tailored to the nature of the sample and the intended purpose of the analysis.

nabidky.nazev: Resistance and durability of building materials
anotace: We offer a comprehensive assessment of the resistance and durability of building materials, focusing on their behaviour under the action of moisture, temperature changes, chemically aggressive environments and biological factors. We investigate the transport and accumulation of water vapour and liquid water, frost resistance, the effects of accelerated ageing and the chemical and biological degradation of materials. Thanks to our laboratory facilities and experience in the long-term assessment of building materials, we can offer not only the tests themselves but also the design of suitable exposure conditions and expert interpretation of the results.

The experimental data can also be used for numerical modelling of transport and degradation processes, which makes it possible to describe the mechanisms taking place in the material in more detail and to predict its behaviour under various exposure conditions. The scope and combination of tests can be tailored to the type of material, its intended use and the required objective of the assessment.

nabidky.nazev: Thermal behaviour of building materials and structures
anotace: We offer a comprehensive assessment of the thermophysical properties of building materials and structures over a wide temperature range (up to 1,600 °C). In particular, we determine thermal conductivity, thermal diffusivity, specific heat capacity, thermal expansion and other thermal properties, including their dependence on temperature and moisture content. The assessment may also include characterization of the phase and structural changes occurring under thermal stress and determination of the residual properties of materials after high-temperature exposure, which makes it possible to assess irreversible changes in the material and its properties after thermal loading.

The measured data can also be used for numerical modelling of heat transfer and coupled heat and moisture transport and for the hygrothermal performance assessment of building structures. For example, we assess thermal resistance and thermal transmittance, thermal bridges, surface temperatures, dynamic thermal behaviour and the heat storage capacity of structures.

nabidky.nazev: Advanced experimental measurement of functional properties
anotace: Characterization and evaluation of the electrical properties of materials in DC and AC electric fields: measurement of DC characteristics (high-precision multimeters); measurement of frequency-dependent AC characteristics (LCR meters), measurement of electrical power output, power input and power factor; measurement of time waveforms, transients and frequency responses (digital/USB oscilloscopes); generation of electrical excitation signals with defined properties (function generators); measurement of surface and volume electrical resistance – assessment of insulating, antistatic, conductive and dissipative materials; monitoring of electrical properties over time (DAS); experimental determination of the self-heating potential of building materials; measurement of thermoelectric properties and determination of the thermoelectric energy harvesting potential of building materials.

We also determine the heat storage parameters of building materials, focusing on their ability to absorb, store and subsequently release thermal energy. In particular, we evaluate specific heat capacity, volumetric heat capacity, thermal conductivity and related thermal characteristics. The results make it possible to compare the heat storage capacity of different materials, optimize their composition and assess their suitability for energy-efficient building structures and applications.

nabidky.nazev: Reactivity and reaction processes of building binders
anotace: We offer a comprehensive assessment of the reactivity and the course of reaction processes of building binders, focusing on their kinetics, the evolution of reaction heat, rheological and technological properties and the formation of reaction products. We monitor changes in phase composition, the evolution of the degree of reaction and the link between chemical processes and the resulting behaviour of the material. Thanks to the combination of calorimetric, rheological and analytical methods, the influence of composition, additions, admixtures or activators on the course of reactions, setting and the development of the binder system can be evaluated in detail.

The experimental results can also be used for modelling chemical and physicochemical processes, which makes it possible to describe the mechanisms taking place in the material and their evolution over time in more detail. The scope of the analyses and the combination of individual methods can be tailored to the type of binder, the composition of the system and the required objective of the assessment.

nabidky.nazev: Environmental assessment
anotace: As part of our services, we calculate carbon footprints and prepare life cycle assessments (LCA), verify the leachability of hazardous substances and the effectiveness of their immobilization, and carry out ecotoxicological assessments. We also focus on the possibilities of meaningfully incorporating waste and secondary raw materials into new materials and production processes.

We assess the environmental aspects of materials and technologies in a broader context. We select the individual procedures with regard to the nature of the material being assessed, its production technology, its intended use and the required purpose of the assessment. The outcome is therefore not necessarily just a set of measured or calculated values. We provide expert interpretation of the data obtained, evaluate their interrelationships and propose optimization options leading to reduced environmental impact, lower consumption of primary resources or the safe use of alternative raw materials.

Our experience applies mainly to cement and other inorganic binders, mortars and concretes, ceramic materials, aggregates, mineral raw materials, construction products, waste materials and secondary raw materials. The scope of the environmental assessment can always be tailored individually – from a targeted assessment of a specific environmental parameter to a more comprehensive assessment of a material, product or technological solution.

nabidky.nazev: Structural survey
anotace: We offer comprehensive structural diagnostics aimed at identifying the causes of defects and designing effective remediation measures. We monitor moisture and its distribution in the structure and carry out laboratory analyses of material composition, including the identification of binders, aggregates and additives.

Based on the measured data and material analyses, we evaluate degradation mechanisms and determine the main causes of defects. We then design suitable remediation measures, taking into account the properties of the original materials, the condition of the structure and its conditions of use.

We can verify the effectiveness of the proposed solutions by numerical simulations of heat and moisture transport, which make it possible to compare individual remediation options and assess their long-term performance.

nabidky.nazev: Research and development of building materials
anotace: We offer support in the development of new building materials and the optimization of existing ones according to the required performance, technological and environmental parameters. We design and optimize formulations with regard to a suitable combination of binders, aggregates, additions, fibres and alternative or secondary raw materials. We also focus on the development of lightweight and sustainable material solutions using natural fibres, renewable raw materials and natural binders, including the design of lightweight and sandwich structures.

The service also includes the optimization of production and technological processes to achieve the required quality, stability and efficiency of the final product. In doing so, we also use advanced manufacturing technologies such as vacuum infusion or 3D printing.

We verify the designed materials and formulations experimentally by determining their physical, mechanical, thermal, hygric and other functional properties. The result is a material or formulation optimized for a specific application and supported by laboratory data.

nabidky.nazev: Numerical simulation of the behaviour of building materials
anotace: As part of our services, we use numerical simulations to analyse and predict the behaviour of building materials and structures, in particular the transport of heat, moisture and salts and its effect on service life and degradation risks. We calibrate and validate the models on the basis of experimental or operational data.

We use the simulation results as computational support for the design and optimization of building materials, construction assemblies and remediation measures. They make it possible to compare alternative solutions, identify critical conditions and predict behaviour in situations where experimental verification is technically difficult, time-consuming or costly.

nabidky.nazev: Testing of protective geotextiles on road slopes using a rainfall simulator
anotace: We offer testing of the erosion protection effect of geotextile materials and other types of technical measures on artificial slopes, such as embankments and cuttings of linear infrastructure or landscaping around residential and civic buildings.

nabidky.nazev: Measurement of stable isotopes of hydrogen and oxygen in waters
anotace: We offer laboratory measurement of stable isotopes of hydrogen and oxygen in waters, both from the natural hydrological cycle (precipitation, runoff in surface streams, soil water and groundwater) and from tracer experiments of any scale (in the landscape as well as in the laboratory) using deuterium at concentrations close to those of natural waters. These determinations make it possible to:
Estimate the residence time of water in a given system (in particular catchments of any scale)
Determine the proportion of event water (e.g. precipitation) and pre-event water (soil water and groundwater) in runoff (e.g. during a flood)
Identify the origin of water in systems (e.g. water damage in a building – whether it is rainwater that has passed through the building or water from a burst water pipe)
Determine the origin of water used in agriculture (isotopic composition of irrigation water vs. soil water and groundwater during the growing cycle)
Assess the behaviour of man-made systems (e.g. the operation of green roofs)

The Stable Water Isotope Laboratory at CTU was established in 2009 and uses the off-axis method (Off-Axis Integrated Cavity Output Spectroscopy). It cooperates closely with the IAEA Isotope Hydrology Section, including participation in four blind tests (WICO) in 2011–2024 with results rated Excellent.

anotace: We offer studies of the sources of eroded sediment and particle-bound phosphorus, from the field scale to large catchments. We prepare a topologically consistent hydrographic network, process digital terrain model (DMR), soil-ecological unit (BPEJ), LPIS, ZABAGED and rainfall erosivity data, and model erosion, sediment delivery to watercourses, and sediment transport and deposition in reservoirs. nabidky.nazev: Monitoring of the water balance of agricultural landscapes
anotace: We offer data from long-term monitoring and quantitative evaluation of the water balance of agricultural landscapes. We measure all the main components of the balance – precipitation, evapotranspiration, discharge and suspended sediment in the receiving watercourse, groundwater level and soil moisture both in the soil profile and at the field scale (cosmic-ray neutron sensors).

The data make it possible to quantify the effect of landscape changes and of nature-based and small-scale technical measures on the water balance, soil water storage, droughts and flash-flood runoff, including co-benefits for the microclimate, biodiversity and soil quality; they are also used to calibrate hydrological models (HYDRUS, SWAT, MIKE SHE) and to assess land management and climate change scenarios.
The quality and continuity of the data are demonstrated by the Nučice experimental catchment (0.531 km²), monitored since 2011, and the open WALNUD database.

nabidky.nazev: Studies of runoff conditions, retention and nature-based measures
anotace: We prepare studies of runoff conditions and the retention potential of the landscape for spatial planning, land consolidation and the preparation of catchment measures. Using data on terrain, soils, vegetation and precipitation, we evaluate the generation and concentration of surface runoff, its volume and peak discharges, as well as the impact of changes in land use or development.

The studies may include rainfall–runoff modelling and spatial assessment of erosion risk using the SCS-CN and SMODERP methods. The outputs are maps of flow paths, sub-catchments, risk locations and retention potential, together with alternative nature-based measures to mitigate floods and droughts, such as floodplain restoration, infiltration and retention features, vegetation strips or changes in the spatial organization of agricultural land.

nabidky.nazev: Determination of erosion characteristics of agricultural soils using the MINI-JET device
anotace: We offer testing of the erodibility of non-cohesive agricultural soils by measuring the critical shear stress with the Jet Erosion Test (JET), using a modified, scaled-down version of the device – the Mini-JET. Measurements are carried out in situ.
The principle of measuring the critical shear stress of the soil is based on monitoring the rate of development of a scour hole eroded by a water jet of known kinetic energy.
The erosion parameters of the soil, such as the critical shear stress and the erodibility coefficient, are calculated from the time course of scour hole development.

nabidky.nazev: Electron microscopy, microanalysis and FIB tomography
anotace: High-resolution scanning electron microscopy (SEM) – detailed study of the morphology, topography and microstructure of materials over a wide range of magnifications; imaging with secondary and backscattered electrons, analysis of surfaces, fracture surfaces, particles, layers, interfaces and microstructural heterogeneities.

EDS – energy-dispersive X-ray microanalysis – qualitative and quantitative determination of chemical composition at selected locations of the specimen, line profiles and area elemental mapping. Identification of chemically distinct phases, inclusions, precipitates, corrosion products and local changes in chemical composition.

EBSD – electron backscatter diffraction – crystallographic and phase characterization of materials, mapping of crystal and grain orientations, determination of grain size and shape, analysis of grain boundaries, texture, misorientations and local changes in crystallographic structure. EBSD data can be correlated with the electron image and EDS elemental analysis.
Combined EDS/EBSD analysis – simultaneous spatial evaluation of the chemical, phase and crystallographic composition of heterogeneous and multiphase materials.

Xe plasma FIB – focused ion beam – precise local material removal and preparation of cross-sections at a selected location of the specimen. The xenon plasma source enables efficient milling of larger volumes of material as well as precise preparation of microstructural details.

FIB cross-sectioning and subsurface analysis – targeted exposure of the subsurface microstructure, layers and interfaces; analysis of internal defects, cracks, pores, inclusions, delaminations and other microstructural flaws that are not accessible by conventional surface observation.

3D FIB-SEM tomography – automated sequential removal of thin layers of material by the ion beam followed by SEM imaging of the individual slices, enabling three-dimensional reconstruction of the microstructure. Particularly suitable for spatial analysis of porosity, cracks, phases, particles and fibres and their interconnection and distribution.

3D chemical and crystallographic characterization – a combination of serial FIB sectioning with EDS and EBSD analysis, enabling spatial evaluation of the chemical, phase and crystallographic arrangement of the material.

Microfabrication and preparation of micro-objects – local FIB milling of specimens, preparation of microbeams, micropillars and other micro-objects for subsequent mechanical or structural experiments; targeted preparation and extraction of samples from a precisely defined location in the microstructure.

Characterization of a wide range of materials – cementitious and geopolymer materials, concretes and mortars, metals and alloys, ceramics, composites, fibrous materials, coatings and thin films, polymers, porous materials, microelectronic structures and other advanced materials.

Comprehensive correlative microstructural analysis – combining morphological, chemical, phase, crystallographic and spatial information from one specific location of the specimen, with the option of progressing from basic SEM observation to a targeted FIB cross-section and 3D reconstruction.
The analyses are available through the dedicated Laboratory of Advanced Microscopy https://mikroskop.fsv.cvut.cz/

reference.nazev: Digitalization and robotization of construction processes – autonomous robotic construction system
reference.poskytovatel: Technology Agency of the Czech Republic (TA ČR)
reference.zamereni: Digitalization and robotization of construction processes
reference.potreba: The main objective of the project was to develop a functional prototype of an autonomous robotic construction system enabling precise and rapid construction with a reduced number of construction workers.
dodali: Autonomous robotic construction system – we developed and validated a functional prototype of a system for the robotization of construction processes (TRL 6).
Robotic bricklaying – we verified the automated construction of masonry structures using an industrial robot.
Robotic 3D printing – we developed and experimentally verified a technology for the 3D printing of building structures from cement-based mixtures.
Linking BIM and robotics – we created a procedure for converting BIM data into inputs for the automated control of robotic construction processes.
Software for robotization in construction – we developed specialized software for the control and programming of robotic construction technologies.
Robotic bricklaying system – we designed and patented a solution for automated robotic bricklaying.
Experimental verification of technologies – we verified the robotic construction technologies on real construction tasks at 1:1 scale.
Integration of robotics and construction technologies – we demonstrated that a robot, construction technology, software and digital data can be combined into a single production system.
reference.prinos: Cooperation with DEK, a major application partner – together we combined research know-how with the practical experience of a construction market leader and verified the developed robotic technologies under real construction conditions.
reference.klicovy_prinos: We demonstrated the practical applicability of robotization in construction by creating and validating a functional autonomous robotic construction system at TRL 6 that links digital data, robotics, specialized software and the actual execution of construction processes.
reference.vice: The work was carried out jointly by the Department of Construction Technology, Faculty of Civil Engineering, CTU, and DEK, a major application partner of the project.

reference.nazev: Development of cement-based and cement-free binders from secondary raw materials
reference.poskytovatel: Ministry of Industry and Trade; Technology Agency of the Czech Republic (TA ČR)
reference.zamereni: Development of cement-based and cement-free binders from coal combustion products and secondary raw materials
reference.potreba: There was a need to reduce the consumption of Portland cement and replace it with binders with a lower carbon footprint and, at the same time, to find technically and economically viable applications for industrial by-products – slags, fly ashes, calcined clays and high-silica wastes – whose composition and reactivity vary considerably depending on their source.
dodali: Methodology for the advanced characterization of input raw materials – we combined the chemical, physical and morphological properties of industrial by-products and natural aluminosilicates into a comprehensive assessment of their composition, structure and reactivity.
Raw material suitability criteria – we established a procedure for determining whether a given material is suitable for producing a binder and by which activation route.
Design of binder systems – we developed binder formulations from characterized precursors, including chemical additives and mechanical activation.
Activation methods – we verified alkali activation, hydraulic activation and the use of pozzolanic reactivity, including the identification of the main reactive phases.
Cement-free mortars and concretes – we verified the performance properties of the developed binders in real material systems.
Practical applications – we demonstrated applicability in precast production, stabilization and solidification, sprayed concrete and land reclamation.
Environmental assessment – we prepared a life cycle assessment (LCA) and input data for environmental product declarations (EPDs).
reference.prinos: Cooperation with industrial partners – ČEZ Energetické produkty, UCT Prague, CEMEX, Heidelberg Materials, Metrostav, Skanska and Weber Saint-Gobain – linked research know-how with real material flows, production technologies and sales channels. The partners provided access to raw material sources as well as to pilot-scale and industrial verification, so the developed binders did not remain in the laboratory but were verified under real production conditions.
reference.klicovy_prinos: We demonstrated that cement-based and cement-free binders with defined performance properties can be purposefully designed from industrial by-products on the basis of the characterization of the input raw material. The result is a sustainable alternative to systems based on pure Portland cement, with reduced CO₂ emissions, higher chemical resistance and a documented environmental profile.
reference.vice: Carried out at the Department of Construction Technology, Faculty of Civil Engineering, CTU in Prague, in cooperation with industrial partners within projects funded by the Ministry of Industry and Trade and TA ČR in 2016–2026.

reference.nazev: Use of combustion products of alternative fuels and biomass in construction
reference.poskytovatel: Ministry of Industry and Trade; Technology Agency of the Czech Republic (TA ČR)
reference.zamereni: Effect of the co-combustion of alternative fuels and biomass on the properties of ash and its use in construction
reference.potreba: The shift of the energy sector from coal to alternative solid fuels and biomass fundamentally changes the composition, phase assemblage and reactivity of the resulting ash. There was a need to describe this change, assess the risks (trace elements, leachability, variability) and determine under what conditions these materials remain usable as a raw material for construction.
dodali: Characterization of combustion process inputs and outputs – we carried out the physical, chemical and morphological characterization of the fuels and the resulting ash.
Description of the effect of co-combustion – we evaluated the influence of coal, alternative solid fuels and biomass on the phase composition of the output materials.
Risk assessment – we carried out mineralogical and morphological analyses and assessed the trace element content and leachability.
Variability assessment – we quantified the variation in material properties caused by fuel composition and operating conditions.
Process optimization – we proposed adjustments to the fuel mix and combustion regime so as to produce ash with the required properties.

Modification of output materials – we verified mechanical, thermal and chemical treatment, alkali activation and the enhancement of pozzolanic reactivity, including control over the formation of amorphous and crystalline phases.

Valorization and circularity – we developed cement-based and alkali-activated materials and verified the recovery of valuable elements from combustion residues, the stabilization of contaminants and long-term durability; we prepared LCAs, input data for EPDs and circularity indicators.
reference.prinos: Cooperation with industrial partners – ČEZ Energetické produkty, UCT Prague, CEMEX, Heidelberg Materials, Metrostav, Skanska and Weber Saint-Gobain – combined the operational experience of energy and cement companies with the research capacity of the department. The partners provided access to real fuel mixes and material flows and enabled the results to be verified at pilot and industrial scale.
reference.klicovy_prinos: We demonstrated that ash from the co-combustion of alternative fuels and biomass is not automatically unusable waste – with knowledge of the combustion process and targeted treatment, it can be turned into a fully fledged construction raw material. The results enable energy companies to maintain sales of their by-products even after the move away from coal, and allow the construction industry to replace part of its primary raw materials.
reference.vice: Carried out at the Department of Construction Technology, Faculty of Civil Engineering, CTU in Prague, in cooperation with industrial partners within projects funded by the Ministry of Industry and Trade and TA ČR in 2016–2026.

reference.nazev: Use of deposited ash – from disposal site investigation to industrial application
reference.poskytovatel: Ministry of Industry and Trade; Technology Agency of the Czech Republic (TA ČR)
reference.zamereni: Investigation of ash disposal sites, processing of the deposited material and its use in construction
reference.potreba: Millions of tonnes of ash, which until now have not been regarded as a raw material, are deposited at the ash landfills and lagoons of energy companies. There was a need to determine exactly what is deposited at each site, how much of the material is actually usable and what technological treatment can turn it into a raw material meeting the requirements of the construction market.
dodali: Disposal site investigation – we carried out a historical and operational analysis of the ash landfills, site surveys, drilling and systematic sampling.

Comprehensive characterization of the deposited material – we determined the mechanical, physical and chemical properties of the material, including its variability across the area and depth of the disposal site.
Estimation of reserves and utilization potential – we quantified the usable amount of material and its suitability for individual applications.
Processing technology – we designed and verified procedures for the technological processing, separation and treatment of the individual components of the deposited material.
Modification of properties – we developed procedures for the targeted modification of the properties of the recovered material according to the requirements of the end application.
Pilot-scale and industrial verification – we verified the proposed technologies at both pilot and industrial scale.
Industrial use – we demonstrated the use of the recovered materials in the production of construction and engineering materials and in land reclamation and remediation.
reference.prinos: Cooperation with industrial partners – ČEZ Energetické produkty, UCT Prague, CEMEX, Heidelberg Materials, Metrostav, Skanska and Weber Saint-Gobain – provided access to real disposal sites, operational data and material flows from power generation, and subsequently enabled the recovered materials to be integrated into the value chains of cement, concrete and building materials production and into real infrastructure and geotechnical projects.
reference.klicovy_prinos: We demonstrated that deposited ash can be systematically reclassified from waste to secondary raw material – from investigation and appraisal of reserves, through technological processing, to industrial use. The result is the substitution of primary raw materials, a reduced environmental burden on the land and a tangible contribution to the circular economy.
reference.vice: Carried out at the Department of Construction Technology, Faculty of Civil Engineering, CTU in Prague, in cooperation with industrial partners within projects funded by the Ministry of Industry and Trade and TA ČR in 2016–2026.

reference.potreba: To develop a building system that makes full use of the physical service life of a reinforced concrete load-bearing structure through the dismantling and reuse of whole undamaged components, instead of their premature demolition followed by mere recycling of the building materials. To develop a building system that reduces the negative environmental impact of the construction industry and limits the carbon footprint of structures while maintaining their high resilience. To develop a building system that can respond to users' changing operational, layout and functional requirements resulting from socio-economic changes in society. To design, develop and experimentally verify the key elements of the demountable system – joints of load-bearing components with controlled stiffness, load-bearing structural elements (walls, columns, beams, floor slabs) and finishing structures (building envelope, partitions, floors, suspended ceilings).
dodali: A unique, qualitatively new multi-purpose demountable precast reinforced concrete building system with controlled joint properties and the possibility of reusing individual components was developed and experimentally verified.

A key part of the development was a patented solution for demountable joints of load-bearing components (linear, planar and volumetric) with controlled stiffness, enabling collision-free dismantling and subsequent reassembly without damaging the connected components.

A technology was developed for high-precision precast reinforced concrete components with embedded steel connectors, allowing dry assembly without wet processes or erection welds, independent of weather conditions.
A solution for the corrosion and fire protection of the joints was experimentally verified.
Original finishing structures (building envelope, partitions, floors, suspended ceilings) using renewable and recyclable materials were developed.

Extensive experimental research (static and dynamic tests) was carried out on individual elements and subsequently on a full-scale (1:1) prototype of the system to verify the spatial stiffness and safety of the structure.
Physical prototypes of the structure were built and used to verify the feasibility of assembly, dismantling and subsequent reassembly.
reference.prinos: The possibility of ‘recycling’ a reinforced concrete structure at the level of whole precast components (reuse), which represents a qualitatively higher degree of recycling than the current recycling at the level of building materials. The proposed demountable precast system enables a significant reduction in material and energy demands (energy-intensive production of cement and steel) as well as in overall costs thanks to the reuse of precast components in a new configuration. The controlled stiffness of the joints and the possibility of optimizing the response of the whole system to dynamic loads ensure resistance to technical, traffic-induced and natural seismicity and improve the indoor environmental quality of buildings through effective protection against vibration and noise. The proposed system also allows a significant reduction in construction time thanks to industrial dry assembly methods and enhances the value of investors' funds through the dismantling, relocation and reassembly of the building according to users' new needs.
reference.klicovy_prinos: A new multi-purpose demountable precast reinforced concrete system was designed, developed and experimentally verified, enabling collision-free assembly, dismantling and reassembly (at a different location, in a different configuration or to a different extent).
reference.vice: The projects were carried out in cooperation between the Faculty of Civil Engineering of the Czech Technical University in Prague (CTU), Prefa Praha a.s. and Metrostav a.s. The individual elements of the load-bearing system and the connectors were designed in cooperation between the Department of Architectural Engineering, the Department of Concrete and Masonry Structures and the Department of Steel and Timber Structures. Static and dynamic tests of the individual structural elements and the experimental prototype were carried out in cooperation between the Department of Architectural Engineering (Faculty of Civil Engineering, CTU), the Technical and Test Institute for Construction Prague, s.p. and the Institute of Theoretical and Applied Mechanics of the Czech Academy of Sciences.

reference.nazev: OOFEM – open-source tool for complex multiphysics simulations
reference.poskytovatel: Czech Technical University in Prague (CTU)
dodali: Object-oriented architecture: OOFEM is built on modern C++ and, thanks to its highly modular architecture, allows researchers to easily implement new material models, finite elements and solvers without having to modify the core of the system.

Advanced multiphysics simulations: Offers an extensive set of solvers for structural mechanics, heat and mass transfer, fluid dynamics and complex coupled problems such as consolidation or thermo-mechanical analyses.

High performance and scalability: OOFEM is designed for computationally demanding problems. It supports parallel computing via MPI and is integrated with advanced direct and iterative sparse solvers such as PETSc, Pardiso and SuperLU.

Modern integration: It can easily be incorporated into modern workflows thanks to extensive Python support, XML-based input and support for Pyodide WebAssembly (WASM) technology, which allows simulations to be run directly in a web browser.
Free and open-source software: OOFEM is distributed under the GNU Lesser General Public License (LGPL). It is free to use, modify and distribute for both academic and commercial purposes.

Extensive library of elements and material models: Contains a wide range of constitutive models, in particular for concrete and soil/fluid interfaces, and supports element formulations ranging from efficient 1D beams and 2D shells (e.g. MITC4) to complex 3D continuum elements.

reference.vice: Joints in steel and timber structures will be of fundamental importance for the transition of load-bearing building structures to carbon-neutral and circular construction. Modern industrial timber structures use steel joints. The project will extend the knowledge of their behaviour, which is essential for advanced modelling. Standards traditionally use analytical procedures that can easily be applied in hand calculations. Advanced modelling by computer simulation using the finite element method is a new discipline for joints in steel structures, and it is very well received in practice for its accuracy and general applicability. Failure is simulated here by reaching the plastic strain limit. This limit depends on physical properties. For a given modelling accuracy, it also depends on the geometry and properties of the model. The project is developing an optimal combination of plastic strain limits for a given model quality for members, joints and their selected components.

Optimization of the 3D printing parameters, ensuring that the instrument is airtight without additional modifications; the total cost of the instrument components is approximately.
Complete documentation (3D models, assembly instructions, software) published in a GitHub repository in line with open-hardware principles (CC0 licence).
reference.prinos: International cooperation with the University of Palermo and a publication in the prestigious Journal of Hydrology.
reference.klicovy_prinos: Low-cost, fully automated and freely available (open-hardware) instrument for measuring the hydraulic conductivity of soils near saturation, usable both in the field and in the laboratory, with potential for wide application, including citizen science. Alternative use of the TMS-4 soil moisture sensor made by the Czech company TOMST s.r.o.
reference.vice: The infiltrometer was developed as a spin-off result of GA ČR project 22-25673S “Hydrological performance of multi-layered constructed soils” – in addition to its main objectives, this basic research project thus also delivered a measuring instrument of practical use. It was developed at the Faculty of Civil Engineering, Czech Technical University in Prague. Publication: Kubát, J.-F., Zanna, F., Mildner, M., Sněhota, M. (2025). Low-Cost Autonomous 3D-Printed Mini Disk Infiltrometer. Journal of Hydrology, 663, 134212.

reference.nazev: Atlas EROZE – model for calculating soil loss and optimizing erosion control measures
reference.poskytovatel: Technology Agency of the Czech Republic (TA ČR)
reference.typ: National applied research; software and methodological output
reference.zamereni: Water erosion modelling and design of erosion control measures
reference.potreba: To create a user-friendly tool for the objective, spatially distributed calculation of soil loss and the design of alternative erosion control measures in complex areas.
dodali: A model based on the spatially distributed Universal Soil Loss Equation (USLE) was integrated into the Atlas DMT environment. It processes detailed terrain models as well as soil and vegetation data, generates map and tabular outputs and allows alternative organizational, agrotechnical and technical measures to be evaluated repeatedly.
reference.prinos: The project combined the research findings of CTU and the Research Institute for Soil and Water Conservation (VÚMOP) with development by the company Atlas and created a practical tool applicable in land consolidation and landscape engineering.
reference.klicovy_prinos: Integrated and standardized calculation of erosion risk and direct verification of the effectiveness of the proposed measures using detailed data on the area.
reference.vice: The result was developed in cooperation between the Czech Technical University in Prague, Atlas, spol. s r.o., and VÚMOP, v.v.i. The 2014 manual contains the theory, the working procedure and worked examples.

reference.nazev: RAIN@FSv ČVUT – design rainfall and data for hydrological modelling
reference.zamereni: Design rainfall, hydrological modelling and direct runoff
reference.potreba: To make available consistent and methodologically documented data for selecting the design rainfall, its temporal distribution and antecedent moisture conditions, and for calculating the runoff response.
dodali: The platform provides 6-hour design rainfall depths for return periods of 2–100 years, six standardized hyetographs at a 5-minute time step, soil and land-use data, and the HydroRAIN-6H and HydroRAIN-CN applications. It also offers WMS, WFS and WPS services for direct use in GIS.
reference.prinos: The platform has provided designers, local authorities, researchers and teachers with a common source of documented data for erosion control and flood protection measures, land consolidation and adaptation planning.
reference.klicovy_prinos: A consistent chain from design rainfall through soil and antecedent moisture conditions to the calculation of direct runoff using the SCS-CN method.
reference.vice: The platform combines web applications and machine-readable GIS services and supports reproducible hydrological calculations for the territory of the Czech Republic.

reference.nazev: Czech Land Use and CN Analyzer
reference.zamereni: Preparation of CN layers and calculation of direct runoff
reference.potreba: To automate the time-consuming and error-prone preparation of consistent layers of land use, hydrologic soil groups and CN values for the SCS-CN method.
dodali: The QGIS plugin downloads and hierarchically combines open ZABAGED and LPIS data and soil layers, creates topologically consistent CN2 and CN3 layers and calculates runoff depth and volume from user-defined or design rainfall. It allows users to insert their own data and scenarios of measures between the individual steps.
reference.prinos: The result is an open, verifiable and reproducible workflow with Czech and English documentation, input validation and automated tests, used in research, design practice and teaching.
reference.klicovy_prinos: Considerably faster preparation of hydrological inputs and transparent comparison of the current state with proposed scenarios of measures.
reference.vice: The tool was developed through inter-departmental cooperation and cooperation with students. The method is described in a peer-reviewed article by Jehlička, Landa and Kavka in VTEI 2/2026, DOI 10.46555/VTEI.2026.01.004.

reference.nazev: WIDER UPTAKE – reuse of treated wastewater for urban greenery
reference.poskytovatel: European Commission – Horizon 2020
reference.zamereni: Water reuse, circular economy, urban greenery, digital data management
reference.potreba: To verify the technical, environmental and operational feasibility of the safe reuse of treated municipal wastewater for irrigating urban greenery and to identify barriers to the wider uptake of water-smart solutions.
dodali: Czech demonstration case study focusing on the irrigation of urban greenery with different water sources
Monitoring and evaluation of water quality and operational data
Digital platform for managing and presenting data from the demonstration sites, including tools for compliance and risk assessment
Supporting materials for assessing the technical, environmental and regulatory aspects of water reuse
reference.prinos: Involvement of the Department of Urban Water Management (K144) in a large European consortium and practical verification of water-smart solutions under Czech conditions, including the integration of experimental data, IoT monitoring and digital tools.
reference.klicovy_prinos: Experimental verification of the practical use of reclaimed wastewater as an alternative source for urban greenery and development of tools for data handling and decision support.
reference.vice: The WIDER UPTAKE project ran in 2020–2024 and focused on the wider implementation of water-smart solutions and circular economy principles in water management.

reference.nazev: Energy-saving fitting for joining two pressure pipes into a single outlet pipe
reference.poskytovatel: Czech Technical University in Prague (patent holder)
reference.zamereni: Pressurized water systems, pumping stations, energy efficiency
reference.potreba: To reduce the local hydraulic losses that occur when joining the discharge pipes of pumps connected in parallel, thereby increasing the energy efficiency and operating economy of pressurized systems.
dodali: New geometry of a junction fitting with two inlet pipes and one outlet pipe
Elliptical transition of the outlet cross-section and an internal flow-guiding element limiting the collision and mixing of the flows
Experimental verification of hydraulic losses for various flow ratios
Technical solution protected by a Czech and subsequently a European patent
reference.prinos: Patent-protected solution applicable in water supply, industrial pressurized systems and spa water engineering (balneotechnics), where it reduces energy losses and operating costs.
reference.klicovy_prinos: The average local loss coefficient of the proposed fitting is approximately 1.2, considerably lower than for conventional flow-junction designs (approx. 2.0–2.9).
reference.vice: European patent EP3910226B1 was granted in 2022. The solution is intended primarily for joining the discharge pipes of pumps operating in parallel.

reference.nazev: Czech Historical Atlas
reference.poskytovatel: Ministry of Culture of the Czech Republic
reference.zamereni: Applied research project in the field of digital and web historical cartography
reference.potreba: To present selected historical topics through historical maps using digital cartography tools. To design the structure and functionality of the web map portal.
dodali: Printed historical atlas focused on 20th-century history
Web map portal focused on 20th-century history, in both Czech and English versions
reference.prinos: New knowledge in the field of historical cartography. A methodology for transferring printed maps to the web environment.
reference.klicovy_prinos: The web map portal, devoted to Czech and Czechoslovak history in an international context, offers experts and the general public, as well as pupils and students, an unconventional approach, not previously implemented in the Czech Republic, to the results of historical research through electronic historical cartography.
reference.vice: The project was carried out in cooperation between the Faculty of Civil Engineering, Czech Technical University in Prague, and the Institute of History of the Czech Academy of Sciences. The main project outputs (the printed atlas and the web map portal) were awarded the Map of the Year prize by the Czech Cartographic Society.

reference.nazev: Vltava – transformations of the historical landscape due to floods, dam construction and changes in land use, with links to cultural and social activities around the river
reference.poskytovatel: Ministry of Culture of the Czech Republic
reference.zamereni: Creating a comprehensive information system (2D and 3D) of the Vltava River based on the processing of a large volume of archival materials (historical documents, maps, plans, photographs) and their combination.
reference.potreba: Design of a procedure for processing materials, especially maps. Design of the information system and its presentation through a map portal combining 2D and 3D data. Design of a method for producing large-format physical models.
dodali: Unique map portal on the Vltava River
Extensive monograph on the transformations of the river from various perspectives
Large-format physical 3D models of the original river valley
reference.prinos: A high-quality web cartographic work respecting the principles of cartographic legibility, clarity and user-friendliness. Bringing together university experts from various disciplines. A successful exhibition that has been repeated many times.
reference.klicovy_prinos: Preserving, documenting and making accessible a large amount of information on the history of the Vltava, including immovable and movable cultural heritage, by means of a comprehensive information system
reference.vice: The project was carried out in cooperation between the Faculty of Civil Engineering, Czech Technical University in Prague, and the Faculty of Science, Charles University. At the Faculty of Civil Engineering, the Department of Geomatics and the Department of Hydraulic Structures were involved.

Experimental verification of the mechanical and physical properties of the designed mix.
Final application – surface shaping of the designed mix with the robotic arm and production of individual cladding tiles that together form a complete image.

reference.nazev: Implementation of a new technology for the monolithic lining of TBM-driven tunnels in civil engineering
reference.poskytovatel: Technology Agency of the Czech Republic (TA ČR) – DOPRAVA 2020+ programme
reference.typ: Programme supporting applied research and innovation in transport – DOPRAVA 2020+
reference.zamereni: Monolithic tunnel lining; new technology; model test; fibre-reinforced concrete; environment
reference.potreba: The main objective of the project was the research and development of a new energy-efficient industrial technology for the monolithic lining of TBM tunnels, offering savings in time, space and transport, and its implementation in underground construction within civil and transport engineering on the Czech and European markets.
dodali: Verification of the newly developed technology, covering the lining concreting process from pumping of the mix to uneven loading by the machine thrust during tunnelling.

The following were verified in detail: pumpability of the steel fibre-reinforced concrete (SFRC) mix into the monolithic lining in terms of filling, rheology, defects, de-aeration and fibre segregation.
Behaviour of the SFRC mix under compression by a hydrostatic pressure of 5 MPa, simulating the TBM thrust cylinders bearing against the monolithic lining.
Behaviour of the lining during hydration, with the accompanying phenomena of autogenous shrinkage and heat of hydration.
Final condition of the monolithic lining after hardening.
reference.prinos: Extended cooperation with the Czech construction industry – HOCHTIEF CZ a.s.
reference.klicovy_prinos: The newly developed monolithic lining technology is a fully fledged and technically justified alternative to the existing solution, as it allows the final lining to be integrated directly into the tunnelling process, simplifies construction procedures, reduces the number of interdependent process steps and at the same time increases the overall reliability and service life of the tunnel structure.
reference.vice: The project was carried out in cooperation with HOCHTIEF CZ a.s.

reference.nazev: Engineered barrier 200 °C
reference.poskytovatel: Technology Agency of the Czech Republic (TA ČR)
reference.typ: Applied research, public call for proposals under the THÉTA programme
reference.zamereni: Deep geological repository for radioactive waste, bentonite engineered barrier, behaviour of materials at temperatures up to 200 °C
reference.potreba: To verify whether a bentonite engineered barrier can function safely over the long term at temperatures of up to 200 °C, whereas existing deep geological repository concepts in the Czech Republic and worldwide assume a limit of 100 °C at the interface with the waste disposal package. To critically assess the long-term durability and integrity of the barrier under extreme thermal loading of 150–200 °C. To verify the behaviour of the Czech Ca–Mg-type BCV bentonite (from the Černý vrch deposit) under real in situ conditions with simultaneous heat flow and natural saturation with groundwater. To obtain reliable experimental data for the calibration and validation of advanced thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) numerical models, which provide key inputs to the long-term safety analyses of the repository.
dodali: Unique full-scale physical model of a disposal position, installed in situ in the granodiorite (a granitic-type crystalline rock) of the Josef Underground Laboratory. The model combines a high-power heater reaching approx. 180 °C at its surface with a comprehensive online monitoring system that continuously tracks the evolution of the temperature, pressure and hydraulic fields.
Proven technology for the long-term, stable and safe operation of an advanced engineered barrier at high temperature.

Laboratory programme focusing on the mineralogy, geochemistry and geotechnical properties of powdered bentonite after long-term heating in a laboratory oven at 200 °C (for up to 47 months) and on its rehydration capacity.

Advanced numerical model based on hypoplasticity, a soil mechanics theory, implemented in the SIFEL finite element software; the model describes the complex THM response of the bentonite seal at high temperatures.
Device for sampling pore water from saturated bentonite (registered utility model), intended for hydrochemical analyses in the final stages of the research.
reference.prinos: Intensive interdisciplinary cooperation and transfer of know-how between academia (Czech Technical University in Prague, Faculty of Science of Charles University), a state research organization (Czech Geological Survey) and the private sector (TERAMED, s.r.o.). A comprehensive multidisciplinary perspective linking geotechnics, numerical modelling, structural geology, hydrogeology, mineralogy, geochemistry and microbiology. A unique set of monitoring data and physical samples from the dismantling of the experiment, which confirmed the excellent mechanical stability of the barrier and made it possible to reproduce the observed processes realistically in numerical simulations. An expanded knowledge base for the safety analysis of the deep geological repository.
reference.klicovy_prinos: The experiment confirmed that the operating temperature limit of the Czech deep geological repository concept can be raised. It is the first in situ experiment of its kind to operate a complete engineered barrier in a high-temperature regime in a real underground environment over the long term. A higher operating temperature allows containers to be emplaced at a higher density, which significantly reduces the overall size of the repository and lowers capital costs while maintaining the safety of the system.
reference.vice: The application guarantor and end user of the results is the Radioactive Waste Repository Authority (SÚRAO). The project ran in 2018–2025 and covered the entire life cycle of the model – design, installation, long-term operation and controlled dismantling.
